prompt: A creator's follower count is modeled by $N(t) = t^3 - 6t^2 + 15t + 100$ (in thousands), where $t$ is months since launch, $0 \le t \le 6$. The count is always increasing. At what time $t$ is it increasing most SLOWLY?
hint: "Increasing most slowly" means the growth rate $N'(t)$ is at its minimum. So you need to minimize $N'$ — which means looking at $N''$.

hints.text: "Increasing most slowly" means the growth rate $N'(t)$ is at its minimum. So you need to minimize $N'$ — which means looking at $N''$.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Warm up: to find where $g(t) = 3t^2 - 12t + 15$ is smallest, set $g'(t) = 6t - 12 = 0$. Here $g$ happens to be $N'$.
$N'(t) = 3t^2 - 12t + 15$ and $N''(t) = 6t - 12$. Set $N'' = 0$ and check it is a minimum of $N'$.
$t = 2$. $N''$ goes from negative to positive there, so the rate $N'$ bottoms out at $t = 2$ (where $N'(2) = 3$ thousand per month).

explanation: Growth rate: $N'(t) = 3t^2 - 12t + 15$. Its discriminant $144 - 180 < 0$, so $N' > 0$ always — the count really is always rising.
To find where the rate is smallest, differentiate again: $N''(t) = 6t - 12 = 0$ at $t = 2$. $N''$ changes from $-$ to $+$, so $N'$ has a minimum there.

Check the endpoints of the rate too: $N'(0) = 15$, $N'(2) = 3$, $N'(6) = 51$. The slowest growth is at $t = 2$ months. That point is the inflection point of $N$: growth slows down until month $2$, then speeds back up.

alternativeExplanations.title: Vertex of the rate parabola
steps: An upward parabola is lowest at its vertex, so the growth rate is smallest at $t = 2$. Same answer without a second derivative.
